projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with James Bassett was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Today is Friday, May 31st, 2002. And right now we are at the John Dingle Veterans Hospital in Detroit, Michigan. And it is at 4646 John R. Street in Detroit. The person I'm interviewing is James Bassett. He was born on December 23rd 1910. And his current address is 4646 John R. The people attending the interview are me, the Interviewer, Brandy Tish; and my Mom is sitting in ________________. My Dad works for the VA hospital. He's a nurse here and I'm his daughter. Okay. I haven't asked you a question again, but what branch of service were you in?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Antiaircraft.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Okay. Antiaircraft. And your rank was almost corporal. Right?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Yeah. Oh well, that's coming up to a corporal. I just can't recall the name of it.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Okay. Oh, where did you serve at?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Oh, now all a bunch of little places overseas like-- the last place where I left from was __________+ I can't--

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Korea?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: France?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: France?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No. Oh, I know it. I just can't recall it.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: That's okay. If you think of it, you just mention it. How old are you?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: You don't want to know that, girl. You run out of here.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: It's okay.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Ninety-one?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Are you going to be 100?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Huh.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Are you going to be 100?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: I don't know about that now.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Do you remember your date of enlistment?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: No?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: I don't remember that.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: That's fine.

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Now, I got it at home; but I just don't remember.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: In which war or wars did you serve at?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Two.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: World War II?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Two, yeah.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Did you sustain any combat injuries?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: No?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Okay. I'm going to start going through a couple questions. Were you drafted or did you enlist?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Drafted.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Really, oh. How did you feel about that?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: How did you feel about being drafted?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Well, at the time, I didn't feel so hot.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: But __________+, but that's the way I had to go.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Yeah. You didn't really have much choice. So tell me about like your boot camp or training experiences. What was that like?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Oh, well, where I was-- I like to recall the name of the place __________+, but it was really so hot _________+. The weather was hot and very hot.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Where was your training at, do you remember?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Well, I went from here to Georgia. I stayed there and went to-- to Georgia. Stayed there I don't know how long; but we left there and we went to Camp Stewart. From there, just on a very little island. I was just trying to think of the name of it, the island. I can't think about knowing.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: That's okay. So, what was your job or assignment in the war?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: I was on a little instrument they called air finder. I don't know about it. __________+ more or less. And it was three of us on it, but I never did learn it; because I couldn't see. My eyes __________+.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: What were wrong with your eyes?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: My eyes were weak. I couldn't-- it was taking pictures of planes in the air and my eyes was weak. I couldn't see the planes to name them. We had one fellow very good.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Did you see any combat?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No. I was in the combat zone, but I never seen no real combat.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: What was your most memorable experience?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: One morning we were out on the field _________+. And we were there and we got up. It was later on we were out grabbing the guns and knives. And we got there, it wasn't nothing. There was planes going over. When we got out there, they gone. We just didn't see-- see nothing. But the one from __________+, he was scared. They-- they surely coming. They coming this time. They coming this time. He just knew them planes was going to land. Them planes kept going.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Were you awarded any medals or citations?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Oh, I had a _________+ medal. __________+ I was a private. I was--- I couldn't think of the word.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Oh, thank you.

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: You know I was a Private in the Army, a Private First Class. And I had something at home now. Hopefully, they didn't throw it away. I got it home __________+. I never really made real-- I didn't make corporal; so that's what I was, Private First Class.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: How did you stay in touch with your family?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Writing letters.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Letters, oh. What was the food like?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Oh, boy. Oh, oh. It was bad. I'll tell you that. In one word-- I mean one word, bad. We didn't have no good food.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: What was your favorite-- what was your favorite meal?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Favorite meal?

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Out of all the bad food?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: I don't know what was my favorite meal. It wasn't much.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Probably didn't even have one. They were bad. Probably didn't have a favorite meal. You probably didn't like many of them?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No. I can't say that I had a favorite meal. The best meal we had would be eggs in the morning. We would have eggs in the morning. That would be the best meal that we would have.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Did you guys have plenty of supplies? Were you guys short on supplies, or did you have enough supplies?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: We always had plenty of supplies.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: That's good.

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Once in a while, once in a while _________+. I can't remember the name of that little island. We were on it and we had plenty of cows over there and horses.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: I like horses.

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Now you wouldn't want no horse meat.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: No. I like riding horses, not eating horses.

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: I mean to eat, not to ride, to eat now.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Was there something special that you did for good luck?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Hmm?

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Was there something special you did for good luck?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: That I what?

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Did you have a lucky charm or any routine you did just for good luck?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: I have a piece of cloth at home I brought from over there from this island. I'm trying to recall the name of it. I can't remember the name of it. I brought it home and I kept it up until 0 now. I don't know-- it's at home I know somewhere __________+.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: How did you entertain yourselves?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: How did you entertain yourselves?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Well, different ways. We had music around there a lot, quite a bit of music around there at night. And the boys always __________+ they always gamble. And those boys would gamble __________+. Of course, I didn't gamble. But that's the way we entertained. I don't know the name of that town, the town that we went to. I don't remember.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: That's okay. Don't worry about it. What did you do while you were on leave?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: What did you do while you were on leave?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Well, I never was on leave that much. I went-- I went home once.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: How long did you serve for?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Well, a little better than three years.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Oh, wow. What did you think of your officers and fellow soldiers?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Well, it was just a mix group, a mix __________+. The officers were prejudiced. I can say that, very much so; but they treated me pretty good. But, you know, we always got along pretty good.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: That's good. Did you make any close friendships while you were in the service?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Oh, you know, you always make some very close friends. There was some very good boys there. You would have to make some good friends. They all wouldn't be.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Did you keep in touch with any of them after the war?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Not after the war, no.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Did you join--

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: I'm sorry. Go ahead.

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: I kept them in mind. _________+ I would love to hear. I saw one. I think one. Yes, that was one after I come home. He came here. I can't think of the name of the town that I went to see-- went to see him.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Did you join a veterans organization after that?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: No. What did you do-- what did you go on to do as your career after the war?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Let me see now. After the war I had gone Army __________+.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Did your military experience influence your thinking about war or about the military in general?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Well, it influence my thinking, but what good would it do? Now that I'm too old. I said they might __________+. It wouldn't make me like the Army no better.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Do you attend reunions?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: No. For the Army, no. I used to.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: You did. So, you get to see all your friends and stuff?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: There wasn't any there.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: Oh, that's sad. Is there anything you would like to add that was not covered in this interview?

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Well, I would love to find that little piece of cloth I got at home. I just can't think of the name of that town. That's where it come from.

sp.speaker: Brandi Tish
sp.p: That's okay. But I really want to thank you for sharing your recollections and everything. I appreciate it so much. And it was very nice meeting you. Thank you. And thank you again. And it was very nice meeting you.

sp.speaker: James Bassett
sp.p: Okay.
